record.tranche_reason: The post reruns the neuron-explanation and activation-simulation procedure from the 2023 paper on GPT-2 XL, with changes to the examples, explanation format, and simulator.
record.gate_note: The post reports explanation-score measurements for sampled GPT-2 XL neurons, including results from simulating activations using generated explanations. It describes the GPT-4 result of over 1,000 of 307,200 neurons (about 0.3%) as the original paper's result, not a result newly obtained here. Values shown only in figures are not transcribed unless also stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The post reruns the 2023 OpenAI explain-and-simulate procedure on sampled GPT-2 XL neurons with a stronger explainer (Opus 5.5). It reports the share of neurons above the 0.8 correlation criterion, which directly bears on V7. The changes are 35 examples, multi-sentence explanations and a direct 0–10 simulator. A single-neuron case study bears weakly on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The author reports Opus 5.5 identifies 3–19% of GPT-2 XL neurons, 8% at the 0.8 criterion, versus 0.3% for GPT-4, a roughly 26x improvement. The author concludes GPT-2 XL is not clean if clean means every neuron can be explained in one sentence. One-shot scores are treated as a lower bound, and the author is optimistic that newer models and explainers will give more clarity.
record.recipe_differences: It follows the 2023 explanation-and-simulation procedure, but uses 35 rather than 5 examples, permits multi-sentence explanations, runs Opus 5.5 as subagents, uses direct 0–10 simulator scores instead of probability-weighted expected values, and tests samples rather than all GPT-2 XL neurons.
record.method_sensitivity: The initial 20-neuron sample was used to develop the pipeline and had a mean score of 0.51; the fresh 30 had a mean of 0.41. A batch of 12 neurons caused a slight simulator-score drop.
record.problems: The evaluation covers only 50 neurons sampled from layers 8–40, not all GPT-2 XL neurons. The pipeline was designed on the first 20 neurons, and the fresh 30 had a lower mean score. The procedure differs from the original in several ways, including example count and simulator scoring. The post gives no uncertainty estimates, and several figure results are not numerically described in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. The original paper's GPT-4 aggregate result is cited background, not a result from this post.

untested.parts: How well explanations fit their source activating examples is never quantified. Only one neuron is examined in depth.
Explainers other than GPT-4 and Opus 5.5 are not tested, nor are models other than GPT-2 XL. Layers outside 8–40 are not sampled, and not all neurons are scored.

missing.what: Shares of neurons above each of the four Fig. 3 criteria. The TLDR gives a 3–19% range; 0.7 and 0.8 are named in the text.
Explainer-vs-simulator decomposition: Opus 5.5 simulating GPT-4 explanations on 10 neurons did better than GPT-4, and the combination was best. This is figure only.

record.verdict_notes: The 0.3% GPT-4 figure is cited from an original source and is not this study's result. The pipeline was designed on the first 20 neurons (mean 0.51 vs 0.41 on the fresh 30), which suggests optimistic bias. The sample is small, there are no uncertainty estimates, and the explainer and simulator are the same model family. The removed V7 limits_scope label had no basis: R2, R3 and R5 show no condition where V7 fails. A commenter (leogao) argues that top+random correlation lacks precision/recall validity, and another notes GPT-2 XL was trained with dropout, relevant to V4. These are comments, not results.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not audit Qwen3-32B neuron poles or measure the shares assigned one job, two related jobs, or not understood.
It tests a sample from GPT-2 XL, not whether one-main-job shares hold across modern dense and mixture-of-experts models or at larger scales.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron or recursive-generalization account is tested.
The post does not test architecture or regularization as causes of interpretability, or estimate interpretability shares for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
It does not test attribution graphs or whether a model's own neurons suffice as circuit units.
The post evaluates explanations generated from top-firing excerpts against simulated activations, but does not separately quantify how well each explanation fits its source excerpts.
The evaluation covers a 50-neuron GPT-2 XL sample and the reported scoring setup; it does not test other explainer models beyond GPT-4 and Opus 5.5 or other language models.
